steps.body: A numeral is a promise written down: make the mark 3 and you promise an amount of three. Writing starts with 1, 2, 3.
steps.narration: A numeral is a promise written down: make the mark 3 and you promise an amount of three. Writing starts with 1, 2, 3.

widget.prompt: Show what the numeral 3 promises — build its amount.

commonCounts.feedback: Two falls short of the promise; the mark 3 names one more than this.
Four overshoots the promise; the mark 3 stops the count at three.

widget.missFeedback: Read the numeral, then build exactly that many.
widget.successFeedback: Three — the mark 3 and this group say the same thing in two languages.

predict.prompt: The mark 3 is written on a card. What does it promise?
predict.reveal: Numerals are names for amounts — the shape carries a count inside it.

cml.actionGoal: Link the written numeral to the exact amount it names for kcw write 123.
invariants: A numeral is a written promise about an amount: it records the last word of a careful count, position gives each digit its job, and the promise survives any change of objects or arrangement — the anchor for kcw write 123.
misconceptions: Treating numerals as decorations, reading digit pairs without position, or matching a numeral to roughly rather than exactly its amount.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If one more thing joined the group, which single mark of the numeral would have to change?

widget.prompt: What is a written numeral, really?

options.label: A promise about how many
options.feedback: Correct — write 3 and you promise a count of three; the mark stands for the amount.

options.label: A little drawing of the things
options.feedback: The numeral 3 looks nothing like three apples — it names the amount, not the objects.

options.label: A decoration for the page
options.feedback: Numerals carry meaning: change the mark and you change the promised amount.

options.label: A letter of the alphabet
options.feedback: Letters build words; numerals name counts — two different writing systems.

hints: Last number said, first mark written.

widget.prompt: Put the three writing moves in order for the numeral 3.

misorderFeedback.feedback: The final step cannot come first. Begin with the amount or starting point, then finish the numeral.

widget.missFeedback: Build the sequence in this order: Start at the top, then Curve to the middle, then Curve to the bottom.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — the stable top-to-bottom path makes a readable 3.

widget.prompt: A group shows 1 dots. Which numeral names that amount?

options.feedback: Correct — the numeral 1 is the written name for a group of exactly 1.
2 promises more dots than the group holds; the count stops at 1.
0 promises fewer dots than the group holds; the count reaches 1.
3 promises more dots than the group holds; the count stops at 1.

widget.prompt: What number comes right after 1? Hop one and tap where you land.

commonLandings.feedback: 1 stops one complete hop too soon. Continue the final 1-unit hop to reach 2.
3 goes one complete hop too far. One hop from 1 lands on 2.

widget.missFeedback: Count 1 on from 1: you land on 2.
widget.successFeedback: 2 — the next numeral in the writing order is the next number in the song.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — a single hop forward reaches 2.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — right after 1 means one hop, stopping on 2.

explanationVariants: The last word is the mark.

widget.prompt: Mia counted three shells but wrote 2. Which numeral corrects her record?

options.feedback: Correct — the last number said, 3, is the one the numeral must record.
The count stopped at 3; writing one more would record a block that is not there.
That records one too few — the count reached 3, so the numeral must too.
That runs two past the count; the written numeral copies the last word said, 3.
